text: You find a cool new app, promising to simplify your day. All you want is to download it and start using it immediately.
Before you dive in, a huge wall appears: 'This app needs access to contacts, camera, location, photos.' A long list of demands, all at once.
Why does a simple game need your calendar? Your gut says this feels wrong, but you just want the app to work.
Here’s the invisible system. Developers know asking later interrupts your flow, making you more likely to say no. Asking once upfront creates less friction.
You've been conditioned to just hit 'Accept.' This means you grant access to things the app might not even need, risking privacy for convenience.
The app works, but you've given up a tiny piece of privacy. Now you see the design pattern exploiting your desire for instant gratification.
